ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Suppression versus secretion clearance

A patient recovering from a respiratory infection asks whether an antitussive and an expectorant perform the same task. The clinician explains that one reduces cough signaling while the other is intended to aid mucus clearance. Which drug belongs to the latter category?

  1. Guaifenesin
  2. Benzonatate
  3. Codeine
  4. Dextromethorphan
  5. Hydrocodone
Answer and explanation

Guaifenesin

Guaifenesin is an expectorant used to aid clearance of respiratory secretions.

Option explanations

Guaifenesin: Guaifenesin is an expectorant used to aid clearance of respiratory secretions.

Benzonatate: Benzonatate suppresses peripheral cough signaling.

Codeine: Codeine is a centrally acting opioid antitussive.

Dextromethorphan: Dextromethorphan is a centrally acting nonopioid antitussive at therapeutic doses.

Hydrocodone: Hydrocodone is an opioid cough suppressant.
